data.current_description:
Encodes your content into a QR image and returns it in the response
body. **Nothing is stored**: no QR code record is created, no UUID is
minted, no redirect through this domain is involved, no audit entry is
written, and the encoded content is not logged.

Every other endpoint here creates a *dynamic* code, which encodes a
`/q/{uuid}` address on this domain and resolves to your destination on
each scan — that is what lets a printed code be re-pointed later. This
one encodes your address directly, so the scanner never touches us. The
trade is the obvious one: **a code rendered here can never be re-pointed,
and it records no scans.** Print it only when that is what you want.

Send either `data` (the literal payload) or `qr_type` plus `content`
(a type described by its fields). The types that resolve to a page this
application serves — social, app, coupon, menu, barcode, gift_giveaway —
are refused here, because there is no version of them that encodes
nothing of ours.

Four advisory headers ride on the response, because an image body has
where to put them: `X-QR-Scannable` (`yes` or `warnings`),
`X-QR-Warnings`, `X-QR-Contrast-Ratio`, and `X-QR-Frame-Omitted` on a PNG
whose design carries a frame or caption.

**Requires the `api_access` plan feature.** Without it this endpoint answers 403 even with valid credentials.
data.description_suggestion: Generates a static QR code image that encodes content directly without creating a database record, UUID, or redirect. Returns the QR image in the response body with advisory headers: `X-QR-Scannable` (yes/warnings), `X-QR-Warnings`, `X-QR-Contrast-Ratio`, and `X-QR-Frame-Omitted`. Static codes cannot be re-pointed after printing and do not record scans. Send either `data` (literal payload) or `qr_type` plus `content`. Application-hosted types (social, app, coupon, menu, barcode, gift_giveaway) are rejected. Requires the `api_access` plan feature.
